E1.evidence: Issue rclpy#881 gives a C++ publisher snippet, the Python listener, and the traceback ending `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte`; maintainer fujitatomoya reproduced it (`ros2 topic echo /topic` -> `Unable to convert call argument '0' of type 'object' to Python object`, https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/881#issuecomment-1020572058).

E2.evidence: The C++ publisher (reporter's `example` package) puts bytes 120..129 into std_msgs/String.data, which are not valid UTF-8; the Python side (rclpy via the message conversion code generated by rosidl_generator_py 0.9.4) decodes every string field with `PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8(..., "strict")`. The failure depends on the encoding of a value crossing the boundary (a publisher sending valid UTF-8 does not trigger it), so it is an interface failure; the fix changes the generated conversion code, not deployment wiring or build configuration.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the C++ publisher's `topic` output feeds `ros2 topic echo /topic` or the rclpy subscription on "/topic" (issue body).

E4.evidence: Observed failure: traceback in rclpy spin ending in `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte` (issue body).

units.name: example
units.revision_basis: The reporter's C++ publisher package is attached to the issue as a tarball (https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/files/7877250/example.tar.gz), not a repository; it is described from the code quoted in the issue body of 2022-01-16. Built against foxy binaries (reporter: ros-foxy-rclcpp 2.4.0-1focal.20211112.191736). The resolution does not change this unit.

units.name: rosidl_generator_py
units.revision_basis: The consumer process is `ros2 topic echo` or the reporter's rclpy script (reporter: ros-foxy-rclpy 1.0.7-1focal.20211112.191643, binaries); the strict UTF-8 decode lives in the std_msgs Python type support generated by rosidl_generator_py, so this unit is described by the rosidl_python revision. The installed rosidl_python version is not stated; on the foxy branch 0.9.4 (2020-12-08) is the last tag before the report date 2022-01-16 (0.9.5 was tagged 2022-01-31), and 0.9.4 contains `"strict"` at both decode sites, so 0.9.4 is inferred. Resolved: the foxy backport of #176, PR #181, merged as 3788639b on 2022-10-18 (first released in 0.9.7).

failed_conditions.quote: There is a heavy mismatch here between the message/C++ types and Python types. `string` is 8-bit data which does not have encoding, neither does `std::string`. Message strings *ought* to be UTF-8, but this is not enforced. But Python strings always enforce an encoding. So it is perfectly possible to publish data from C++, which gets mangled when received in Python.

loudness_evidence: The mismatch is reported when the two units connect: the consumer logs an incompatibility error naming the element before any data is exchanged.

resolution.summary: Generated Python type support decodes string fields with the "replace" error mode instead of "strict" (rosidl_python #176 on rolling; foxy backport #181, 3788639b), so invalid bytes are replaced instead of raising.
resolution.evidence: fujitatomoya showed the same diff working with his own publisher (ros2_test_prover prover_rclcpp rclpy_881.cpp, commit dc2cb27a) on a rolling source build (ros2/ros2 4a36f319): "it can change the behavior as following w/o `UnicodeDecodeError`." followed by `ros2 topic echo /topic` printing `data: "Hello, xyz{|}~\x7F��!"` (https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/881#issuecomment-1020574514). That is a different peer and distribution; the reporter's foxy composition with the backport was not shown working. jacobperron: "With https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/pull/176 merged, I believe this issue is resolved for Rolling." (https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/881#issuecomment-1209995906).

notes: Class `representation_convention`: the encoding of the string value crossing the boundary (arbitrary bytes from C++ vs strict UTF-8 decode in Python). jacobperron cites the design doc: "If a `string` or `wstring` field is populated with the wrong encoding then the behavior is undefined." (https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/881#issuecomment-1209988539), so the provider is also outside the documented convention; the maintainers resolved it on the consumer side. The consumer unit is named after rosidl_generator_py because the fix changes its generated code; the running consumer is rclpy/ros2cli (foxy binaries), and std_msgs must be regenerated with the fixed generator. fujitatomoya's reproduction (rolling, prover_rclcpp rclpy_881 publisher, public in fujitatomoya/ros2_test_prover at dc2cb27a) is a second composition of the same failure; its rclpy raw=True subscriber receives the bytes without decoding. The fix was also backported to galactic (#180) and humble (#179). I did not download the reporter's tarball; the provider section quotes only the code in the issue body.
